title: Data Migration Engineer
description:
This is a remote position.
The RIS Data Migration Engineer is responsible for overseeing and executing the migration of data between Radiology Information Systems (RIS), ensuring data integrity, accuracy, and compliance with regulatory standards. The Data Migration Engineer will work closely with IT, clinical, and administrative teams to ensure seamless transitions of data from legacy systems to modern platforms, while optimizing workflows and maintaining the highest standards of patient data privacy and security.

• Develop and execute comprehensive strategies for RIS data migration.

• Collaborate with stakeholders to gather and analyse migration requirements.

• Extract clinical, operational, and administrative data from legacy RIS systems.

• Assess and map legacy data structures, including patient demographic records, diagnostic radiology reports, scanned documents, and future appointments.

• Assist in assembling and loading RIS system’s master lists including referring physicians, insurance providers, procedure codes, billing codes, organizational structures such as practices, sites, and rooms, and other master look-up tables.

• Use ETL tools to clean, transform, and prepare data for migration.

• Provide post-migration support for product go-live implementations.

• Partner with cross-functional teams, including customers, IT staff, compliance officers, and third-party vendors.

• Document the entire migration process, including methodologies, tools, and reports.

• Train staff on how to manage, access, and use data in the new RIS system.

• Perform comprehensive validation to ensure data completeness and resolve inconsistencies.

• Conduct post-migration verification and prepare detailed reports for stakeholders.

• Identify and resolve migration-related issues, such as data inconsistencies or system compatibility challenges.

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, healthcare informatics, or related field; or equivalent professional experience

• 3+ years proven experience in data migration within a healthcare environment

• Hands-on experience with data manipulation and/or migration within RIS, PACS, HIS, and EMR systems.

• Proficiency in ETL processes, database structures, SQL, and healthcare data standards.

• Proficient SQL skills and experience with database management.Proprietary software product is supported by MS SQL Server.Proficiency with Transact SQL, triggers, functions, stored procedures, database schema design, SQL agent jobs, and ad hoc querying.

• Using skills above, work with various formats of data such as CSV and other delimited text files, Excel data, SQL databases, Word docs, BMP/JPG files, PDF files. Ad hoc manipulation such as converting one format to another, rename files, move files, parse files, clean data.

• Excellent technical communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively communicate with stakeholders at all levels of the organization

• Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities

• Ability to adapt to constantly changing projects.This role requires a high level of self-motivation, self-management, initiative, and the ability to prioritize multiple tasks effectively.Occasional off-hours work is required to migrate during off-peak system times.

• Attention to detail with a commitment to data accuracy and security.Comfort and willingness to handle and analyze and scrutinize large medical record datasets is a critical aspect of the job to maintain high data quality standards

description:

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Familiarity with MIL-STD-882E and other relevant safety standards

• Strong background in safety analysis techniques including FTA, FHA, SCFTA, and FMECA

• Experience with requirements decomposition for Safety

title: Senior Product Manager
description:

The hydrocarbon industry keeps the world running. But its complexity has left operators tied to legacy systems,making critical decisions on less than 10% of available data. We built Orbital to change that. It’s a foundation modelbuilt specifically for energy that lets companies use AI at scale, harnessing all of their operational data and optimising in real time for any metric. Decisions get faster, operations get safer, and carbon intensity falls.
We’ve raised over $32 million, including one of the largest seed rounds for an AI company in the UK. We’re justgetting started.
The Role
Product Manager’s are responsible for product adoption, usage and value-generation. This means deeply understanding users and their technical requirements and owning delivery for a core area of Orbital. This is a customer- and domain-led role: you’ll spend real time with operators in petrochemicals to understand how decisions actually get made today, and translate that understanding into product capabilities and features that change how their plant is run.
This is a product delivery role. You’ll work closely with AI researchers, ML engineers, full stack engineers, project managers and account managers to invent new capabilities that change how the energy industry is run.
What You’ll Own

• Deep understanding of users, their problems, what matters to them and how they make decisions

• Product strategy and roadmap for your area of Orbital

• Strong working knowledge of downstream operations and the workflows Orbital needs to fit into

• Prioritisation decisions, balancing customer feedback against hypotheses of what will best drive impact

• Requirements, specs, and acceptance criteria

• Ongoing iteration and testing with engineering and research colleagues

• Close relationships and feedback loops with customers and users

• Product, usage and utilisation analytics

Must-Have Qualifications

• 5+ years as a Product Manager, ideally in enterprise B2B SaaS or deep-tech

• Experience with physics, chemistry, heavy industry, manufacturing or AI, UI/UX and workflows

• Direct experience in Oil & Gas or Energy, ideally downstream (refining, petrochemicals)

• A track record of inventing tech products

• Comfort operating with ambiguity, incomplete data, and evolving customer needs

• Clear, structured written and verbal communication - able to represent customer needs to a technical audienceand technical trade-offs back to customers

Nice to Haves (You’ll Learn)

• Experience building AI products - where the product is powered by in-house trained models

• Experience building agentic workflows and agentic product experiences

• Exposure to enterprise delivery environments

• Experience with process control, operations, or reliability engineering software

How We Work

• Process exists to serve delivery, not the other way around

• Pragmatism beats dogma; we adapt tools and rituals to reality

• We value clarity, speed, and ownership over perfect frameworks

• We iterate on process the same way we iterate on product

What This Role Is Not

• Not a delivery or operations role tracking sprint mechanics - that’s Product Operations

• Not a Scrum Master

• Not a passive requirements-taker; this role sets direction

• Not detached from the field - you’ll spend meaningful time with customers and operations teams

Core Responsibilities
Customer & Domain Expertise

• Spend regular time with customers - onsite where useful - to learn about their problems and understand their world

title: Embedded Firmware Engineer
description:
Karman is a fast-growing NVIDIA-backed AI company enabling AI data centers to dynamically orchestrate power and unlock more compute capacity from existing energy infrastructure. For over a decade, we have applied AI to the electric grid - bringing real-time visibility and power-flow control to complex energy infrastructure. Our Karman platform, built on a custom NVIDIA module, brings that same capability to AI data centers, giving operators a way to better use the power already available to them.

We are seeking an Embedded Firmware Engineer to develop production-grade firmware for power grid edge computing platforms. You will work alongside a diverse team of experts across hardware, cloud infrastructure, and AI/algorithms to design, implement, and deploy embedded systems running on mission-critical power infrastructure. This role focuses on hands-on development across multiple hardware variants - writing firmware features, extending our CI/CD and test infrastructure, building logging and diagnostic tooling, and supporting hardware bring-up under the guidance of senior engineers. title: Strategy & Operations Senior Manager
description:
About SafeRide Health

Getting to the doctor should never be the reason someone goes without care. SafeRide Health exists to remove that barrier. We are a technology and services company rebuilding non-emergency medical transportation, pairing our own technology with a national network of vetted transportation providers so that payers and health systems can get members to dialysis, chemotherapy, behavioral health, and primary care reliably and affordably.
It is a rare combination of things to work on: measurable, real-world impact on people who need it, wrapped inside a genuinely hard technology and logistics business. Every single trip involves a member, a clinical need, a provider, a network, a payer contract, and a cost curve. Getting all six right at the same time, at national scale, is the problem we get to work on.
We serve the largest Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, and provider programs in the country. We are a Series C company at approximately $750M in annual run rate with 300+ employees, growing quickly and, unusually for this stage, meaningfully profitable. That last part matters more than it sounds: it means we can build for the long term rather than sprint toward the next raise, and it means the decisions you help make here have real money attached to them.
The industry is moving too. Benefit designs keep shifting, payers are under genuine cost pressure, and the tooling for running a national transportation network (routing, forecasting, automation, AI in the contact center) is far better than it was two years ago. Very little about how this business should be run is settled yet. That is the fun part.
The team you would join
Strategy & Operations is SafeRide's internal consulting team. We are who the company calls when a problem is ambiguous, cuts across several functions, or needs an answer that nobody currently owns.
In a given quarter that can mean rebuilding the economics of how we mix transportation modes, redesigning how the contact center forecasts and staffs itself, working out whether an AI tool actually solves the problem before anyone spends money building or buying it, working out why a client's margin bends the wrong way in month four, or standing up the operating model for a new line of business. The work sits where healthcare, logistics, and technology meet, which is not a combination you find in many jobs, and it comes with unusual access: this team sees the whole P&L and works directly with the leaders who own it.
One thing makes us different from an external consulting firm. Our clients are internal, so we do not hand over a deck and leave. We stay until the change is live, adopted, and visible in the number. A brilliant analysis nobody adopts is a failed project here, which means the job is as much about judgment, communication, and persistence as it is about analytical horsepower.
Increasingly, that work sits between Operations, Product, and Data Engineering. SafeRide is in an exciting growth phase, streamlining how the business runs and leaning into newer, faster technology, including AI, agentic tools, and better data infrastructure, and S&O is where operating needs get turned into clear product and data requirements. The people who thrive here are technically fluent operators: comfortable in the data, able to translate a messy operating problem into something Product and Engineering can build, and credible on both sides of that table.
How we work
We are fully remote and have been from the start, with the team distributed across the US. In practice that means asynchronous by default, written thinking over standing status meetings, and real autonomy over how and when you do your best work. What we ask in return is clarity: say what you are working on, say what you found, and say what you think should happen next.

Lila is hiring an Associate Director/Director, Inference Engineering to lead the team responsible for Lila's model serving platform: the inference APIs, serving frameworks, request routing, batching strategies, and deployment systems that bring models reliably to production.

• Partner with ML, research, and product engineering to make new models production-ready

• Build systems for model onboarding, deployment safety, evaluation gates, and observability

• Build, mentor, and retain a high-performing engineering team, and own the serving roadmap

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Deep understanding of the inference stack for large language models, including serving frameworks (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, TGI), batching strategies, memory constraints, and latency/throughput tradeoffs

• Experience owning a customer- or product-facing API service end to end, including SLAs, incident response, and service reliability in fast-moving environments

Role Overview: We are looking for a Forward Deployed Software Engineer (FDSE) who thrives at the intersection of high-level architecture and deep-stack technical execution. This isn't a "one-off" integration role. You are a hybrid of a software engineer, product strategist, and technical consultant. You will embed with our most strategic customers to solve their most complex problems. However, your mission is dual-purpose: while you deliver immediate value to the customer, you are simultaneously acting as a product scout. You will identify patterns in customer needs and translate those into scalable, core features for our SaaS platform.
What You'll be Doing:

• Lead the design and implementation of new features in our core SaaS product. You aren't just building for one user; you are building for the platform.

• Work across the entire stack, from optimizing database queries and API endpoints to crafting intuitive UI/UX.

• Architect production-ready integrations and workflows. You will lead technical workshops with stakeholders to define "future state" solutions.

• Write high-quality, type-safe, and maintainable code in TypeScript, leveraging modern React and Next.js patterns for performance and scalability.

• Prevent "bespoke bloat." Identify universal customer needs and collaborate with product and engineering teams to bake those into the core technical direction.

• Contribute to CI/CD, testing, and performance monitoring to ensure the stability and reliability of your deployments.

• Mentor teammates and establish engineering best practices to level up the entire team’s output.

Who You Are:

• You think in terms of scalability. When you build a solution for one customer, you’re already thinking about how it could benefit the next ten.

• You take 100% ownership of the success of your deployments. You don't wait for a ticket; you find the bottleneck and fix it.

• You are as comfortable whiteboarding a system diagram for a CTO as you are submitting a pull request for a mission-critical API endpoint.

Experience Requirements:

• 7+ years of professional experience in full-stack or frontend development, specifically within SaaS products or startup environments.

• Strong coder with shown proficiency in TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Java, C++, or similar.

Salary Range: $400,000 - $600,000
About Spectrum Healthcare Partners
Spectrum Healthcare Partners is a Maine-based, physician-owned and led healthcare organization that combines strong physician leadership with expertise from a multi-disciplinary management team. Spectrum is comprised of over 200 Board Certified physicians, including anesthesiologists, pathologists, physiatrists, radiologists, and radiation oncologists, serving patients and communities throughout Maine and northern New England. The care and treatment of our patients is of primary importance to us. Our physicians are dedicated to excellence in the diagnosis, prevention and treatment of illness, lifelong learning, and serving our communities.

title: Security GRC Lead TL1
description:
Job title: Security GRC Lead

Location: London or Bristol 

Level: TL1

Team: Security 

Contract: Permanent

Reporting To: Head of Information Security 

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.

 

About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

 

Where in the world of Kaluza will I be working? 

You'll be joining the Information & Cyber Security team, a core part of our Platform & Security Engineering organisation. Security at Kaluza isn't a silo - you'll work closely with colleagues across security engineering, identity and access management, platform engineering and enterprise technical services.

As the Security GRC Lead, you will serve as the accountable operational owner for Kaluza’s Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance capability. You will establish and maintain a unified Common Control Framework, lead regulatory and framework readiness (including SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, and ISO 22301), and work with engineering teams to demonstrate effective implementation of controls.

A core focus of this role is acting as the primary information security bridge to Kaluza’s central Risk & Compliance team. You will closely collaborate with them to assess the impact of evolving security and privacy regulations, ensuring regulatory risks are clearly quantified, actionable, and seamlessly integrated into the wider enterprise risk framework.

What you will be doing

- Regulatory Impact & Horizon Scanning: Collaborate closely with the Risk & Compliance team to monitor, evaluate, and interpret emerging regulatory changes in the information security, privacy, and critical infrastructure domains.

- Security Impact Assessments: Translate complex regulatory developments into actionable security control requirements and risk assessments for Kaluza, specifically covering:

- Sector & Critical Infrastructure Regulations: NIS2, AESCSF, NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF), and the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill.

- Emerging Tech & Governance Standards: AI management and governance expectations (ISO 42001).

- Enterprise Risk Integration: Partner with Risk & Compliance to ensure security and resilience risks, control gaps, and regulatory exposures seamlessly flow into and align with the enterprise risk management (ERM) framework. Maintain high data accuracy across the security risk register to support board-level visibility.

- Common Control Framework: Design, build, and maintain a single Common Control Framework (anchored initially on ISO 27001 Annex A) mapped across all regulatory, framework, and client contractual requirements.

- Standards & Policy Suite: Help continuously improve Kaluza's security policy and standards library.

- Continuous Control Monitoring: Shift Kaluza from point-in-time evidence gathering to automated control monitoring using commercial GRC platforms (e.g., Vanta), making audit readiness a natural byproduct of daily operations.

- SOC 2 Type 2 Programme: Lead the gap assessment, control build-out, and sustained observation period required for Kaluza’s SOC 2 Type 2 commitment.

- Standards Maintenance: Oversee continuous alignment with ISO 27001 and ISO 22301 to prevent posture drift between annual audit cycles.

- Governance

title: Senior Data Scientist
description:
Senior Data Scientist | Autoplanner | Hybrid Working | London

Introduction:  

We are Ocado Group, and we're bringing world-class automation to online grocery. Our Ocado Smart Platform (OSP) combines cutting-edge robotics, AI, and IoT within our advanced CFCs (Customer Fulfilment Centres). We've mastered the single pick, transforming online delivery for our global partners. Join us and be part of a team pushing the boundaries of retail technology.

About the Role:

As a Senior Data Scientist within our Autoplanner team, you will build AI-powered systems that unify planning across global warehouses and last-mile operations. You will be responsible for developing the machine learning models, optimisation algorithms, and operational simulations that underpin our core planning products. By taking high-impact models from concept through to monitored production systems, you will ensure automated operational plans are robust, globally optimised, and trusted to run live across our partners' international supply chains.

Working closely with cross-functional software engineers and product managers, you will set the technical direction for key initiatives while mentoring colleagues to elevate the team’s overall data science capabilities. You will also engage directly with internal and external stakeholders, including global retail partners - to translate complex logistics challenges into production-ready data science solutions, shaping the future of autonomous operational planning.

Key Responsibilities:

• Deliver machine learning models for planning products, iterating from initial prototype to evaluated and monitored production artefacts.

• Explore innovative modelling and optimisation approaches, benchmarking and testing them rigorously against existing solutions.

• Build and extend simulations of warehouse operations and customer demand to validate and power live operational plans.

• Define and measure business-critical metrics using robust statistical techniques, establishing the team's standards for model evaluation.

• Set the technical direction and delivery strategy for the data science initiatives you lead.

• Develop the technical capabilities of data scientists across the team through mentoring, technical guidance, and collaboration.

• Partner with software engineers to ensure models are cleanly packaged, deployed, monitored, and efficiently served on the platform.

• Own relationships with product managers, internal partner teams, and external retailers to align on requirements and delivery roadmaps.

What We’re Looking For: Essential

• Proven track record of taking data science and machine learning models into production, maintaining them, and leading initiatives end-to-end.

• Strong machine learning and statistical expertise, including the ability to evaluate model performance rigorously against business metrics.

• Fluency in writing production-quality Python code.

• Experience querying and working with large datasets in cloud data warehouses such as BigQuery, including implementing data-quality checks.

• Experience building simulations or stochastic models of operational systems.

• Practical experience using AI coding agents, alongside the critical judgement to verify and test generated code and outputs.

• Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with software engineers, product managers, and diverse business stakeholders.

Nice to Haves

• Experience with mathematical optimisation frameworks and toolkits, such as OR-Tools.

• Experience with discrete-event simulation libraries, such as SimPy.

• Background or domain knowledge in logistics, supply chain, or operational research.

Benefits  

We believe in supporting our people with meaningful, flexible benefits that prioritise well-being and work-life balance. Here’s a snapshot of what you can expect:

• Time to recharge: 25 days annual leave (rising to 27 after 5 years), plus the option to buy more - and 30 days a year to work from anywhere

title: Redwood Finance Automation Engineer, Italy
description:
Redwood Finance Automation Engineer, Italy
Contract: Duration being confirmed. Start: 15 November 2026. Location: Remote, for consultants based in Italy. Day rate: EUR 350 a day. Language: English.
The programme
An established organisation is automating its finance operations on Redwood Finance Automation. The work covers the record-to-report cycle: the period-end close, account reconciliation, journal processing and the reporting that follows, all connected to the organisation's ERP.
You will build what the solution design sets out. You will configure the close and reconciliation processes, build the integrations with the ERP and the systems around it, and carry each process through testing, go-live and early support.
What you will work on
Close processes built and configured end to end: task lists, dependencies, approvals and the automated steps between them. Automated account reconciliation, including matching rules and exception handling. Journal entry automation, from data preparation and validation through to posting in the ERP. Integration with SAP S/4HANA or ECC and other source systems, through standard connectors, file and API interfaces. Intercompany, accrual and reclassification steps automated alongside the close. Workflow logic in REL or JavaScript where the standard designer does not meet the requirement. Unit and integration testing, defect fixing, and support through user acceptance testing. Promotion between environments, cutover and hypercare. Technical documentation and handover to the support team.
What you bring
Hands-on delivery on Redwood Finance Automation (RunMyFinance), where you built close, reconciliation or journal processes yourself on at least one live implementation. 5 or more years in finance systems or automation engineering. Working knowledge of SAP FI/CO postings and master data, or the Oracle equivalent, and where ERP integrations tend to break. Workflow scripting in REL or JavaScript, and hands-on ERP integration. A finance-side understanding of the record-to-report cycle and month-end controls.
Useful but not essential:
Redwood RunMyJobs workload automation. BlackLine, Trintech, or SAP Advanced Financial Closing. A current Redwood certification. Financial services or another regulated industry, including work under SOX or similar audit controls.
How to respond
Apply with your CV and your available start date. With it, add three lines on your most recent Redwood implementation: the finance processes in scope, the ERP it connected to, and what you built yourself.
About Yadimen
Yadimen Consulting Limited is an IT consulting company focused on financial services. For this programme we are putting experienced Redwood Finance Automation people in front of the client.
